newsitem.title: FINLAND: LONDON ANALYSTS SAY UP NOKIA ESTIMATES.
newsitem.headline: LONDON ANALYSTS SAY UP NOKIA ESTIMATES.

text.p: London based analysts on Tuesday said they raised their forecasts for Finnish telecommunications group Nokia after it beat forecasts for first-half earnings, and they issued or reiterated positive recommendations on the stock.
Morgan Stanley raised its forecasts for Nokia EPS to 18 markka this year and 21.15 markka in 1998 from 17.04 markka and 20.31 markka respectivey, analyst Gareth Price-Jones said.
Morgan Stanley maintained its outperform recommendation and set a 550 markka 12-month price target, he said.
Finnish Merita's London-based Nokia analyst Matthew Lloyd said he would probably raise his 1997 EPS forecast from 16.60 markka, and changed the short term recommendation to outperform.

Longer term, Nokia's margins may come under pressure amid tougher competition in handsets and mobile phone usage would fall, squeezing operators' margins and infrastructure prices, so the long term stance was neutral, Lloyd said.
But short-term, Nokia would be supported by positive factors such as healthy margins and a new palm-sized handset to compete with Motorola's and Ericsson's top products, he said.

Lehman Brothers analyst Jeremy Alun-Jones said he upgraded his EPS forecasts to 18.20 markka this year from 16.20 previously and to 21.80 markka next year from 18.50, and reiterated his outperform stance on the stock.

The three main reasons for the upgrade were stronger than expected handset margins in the first half, other operations which boosted the second quarter, and strong operating cash-flow at 4.2 billion markka "over twice what I predicted for the full year," Alun-Jones said.
CSFB said it upped its estimate for Nokia EPS to 18.5 markka this year and 23 markka next year from 17.1 and 22.1 markka respectively, rating the stock a buy.
JP Morgan said it also rated Nokia a buy with a price target of 550 markka.

Before Nokia on Monday reported first-half earnings, EPS estimates supplied by Edinburgh Financial Publishing to the Reuters Securities 3000 system on July 25 ranged between 13.62 markka and 16.45 markka for this year and between 15.45 and 22.8 markka for next year.
Nokia's first half EPS was 8.49 markka compared to a median estimate of 8.00 markka in a Reuters poll. The highest estimate was for 8.40 markka EPS in the first half.
